case_title: K.A. Kotrappa Reddy and Anr. v. Rayaramanjujuna Reddy@N.R. Manjuna
confession: Extra-judicial confession made to PW14 (B.M. Halaswamy)
aggravating_circumstances: Formation of unlawful assembly, use of dangerous weapons, presence of numerous witnesses
mitigating_circumstances: Delay in lodging FIR, delay in sending seized articles to FSL, delay in post-mortem report, presence of non-partisan witness
trial_court_outcome: Convicted accused Nos. 1-9 for offences punishable under Section 143, 148 and 302 read with 149 IPC; Accused No. 10 found guilty of the offence punishable under Section 114 read with 302 IPC; Accused Nos. 2, 4 and 9 also convicted for the offence punishable under Section 324 IPC; Acquitted accused Nos. 11 and 12
high_court_outcome: Acquitted accused Nos. 1-10 and upheld acquittal of accused Nos. 11 and 12
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were involved in a dispute over road repair work. The accused formed an unlawful assembly, carried dangerous weapons, and abused and beat the victim, resulting in his death. The victim was taken to a hospital where he was declared dead. The FIR was lodged several hours after the incident. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovered weapons. However, the High Court found the evidence unreliable due to the presence of interested witnesses, delays in reporting, and inconsistencies in the investigation. The accused claimed an alibi, which was supported by independent witnesses.
